title: History Of Video Game Consoles | Atari To PlayStation, Xbox, Switch And Switch 2 | Gaming Explained
description: A timeline of home video game consoles from the Magnavox Odyssey in 1972 to the PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and Nintendo Switch 2, with launch dates and sales records.

sections.heading: From a box with dots to your living room
sections.script: Every gaming era has its box under the television. In this video we trace the history of video game consoles, from the very first home machine to the handheld hybrids of today. We follow the big three, Nintendo, Sony and Microsoft, along with the companies that shaped them, such as Magnavox, Atari and Sega. Along the way we look at launch dates, record breaking sales and the ideas that changed how we play. A quick note on numbers. Console sales come from company reports and are updated regularly, so we will say when each figure was announced. Dates come from the console articles on Wikipedia and from company announcements. Plug in, press start, and let us go back to the very beginning.

sections.heading: The Magnavox Odyssey in nineteen seventy two
sections.script: The first commercial home video game console was the Magnavox Odyssey. The hardware was designed by a small team led by Ralph Baer at Sanders Associates, and Magnavox released it in the United States in September nineteen seventy two. It was a simple machine. It could show three square dots and one line on a black and white screen, and players put plastic overlays on the television to create the game worlds. The idea was revolutionary. For the first time a family could connect a box to the television and play a game together in the living room. Every console that followed builds on that big idea.

sections.heading: Atari and the age of cartridges
sections.script: Next came the cartridge. The Atari 2600 was released around September nineteen seventy seven as the Atari Video Computer System. It popularised microprocessor based hardware and games stored on swappable ROM cartridges, a format first used by the Fairchild Channel F in nineteen seventy six. The system came with two joysticks and a game cartridge, and Atari renamed it the Atari 2600 in November nineteen eighty two. Swappable games changed everything. Instead of owning a machine that did one thing, you could buy a new game and have a whole new experience. That business model, selling the console and then selling the games, is still how the industry works, and Atari helped turn gaming into a mainstream family hobby.

sections.heading: Nintendo and Sega fight in the eighties
sections.script: The Nintendo Entertainment System began as the Family Computer, or Famicom, in Japan on July fifteenth, nineteen eighty three. It reached American test markets on October eighteenth, nineteen eighty five, followed by a nationwide launch on September twenty seventh, nineteen eighty six. It was Nintendo's first programmable home console and competed mainly with Sega's Master System. Sega then launched the Mega Drive in Japan in October nineteen eighty eight, and it came to North America as the Genesis in August nineteen eighty nine. Nintendo also changed handheld gaming. The Game Boy launched in Japan on April twenty first, nineteen eighty nine, and reached North America on July thirty first of that year. Super Mario, Sonic and Tetris became household names.

sections.heading: PlayStation changes the game
sections.script: In nineteen ninety four a new player entered the arena. The Sony PlayStation was released in Japan on December third, nineteen ninety four, then in North America on September ninth, nineteen ninety five, and in Europe on September twenty ninth that year. It competed with the Nintendo sixty four and the Sega Saturn. The PlayStation used discs instead of cartridges, which made games cheaper to produce and let developers add video and music. Nintendo's console arrived in Japan on June twenty third, nineteen ninety six, and in North America on September twenty ninth that year. Sega's Dreamcast came in Japan on November twenty seventh, nineteen ninety eight, as the last home console Sega ever made. The stage was set for Sony to become a giant.

sections.heading: PlayStation Two the all time champion
sections.script: The PlayStation Two launched in Japan on March fourth, two thousand, and reached North America on October twenty sixth that year. It competed with the GameCube, the Dreamcast and the Xbox. It also became the best selling console of all time. Wikipedia and many news sites repeated a figure of more than one hundred fifty five million units for years, and Sony has since stated that the console sold more than one hundred sixty million units in its lifetime, as reported by Gamereactor and Heise. Its library of games was enormous, and it stayed on sale for many years. Even today, nothing has beaten it as the all time sales leader, although the Switch has come close.

sections.heading: Microsoft joins with Xbox
sections.script: In November two thousand one, a software company decided to build a console. The original Xbox was released by Microsoft on November fifteenth, two thousand one in North America, then in Australia, Europe and Japan in two thousand two. It was the first major American made console since the Atari Jaguar in nineteen ninety three, and it competed with the PlayStation Two and the GameCube. The Xbox set Microsoft up for the next generation. That later generation included the Xbox three sixty, which Microsoft officially unveiled on May twelfth, two thousand five, in a special program called Xbox The Next Generation Revealed. From then on, the console market had three major players.

sections.heading: The Wii and the casual boom
sections.script: Nintendo took a very different path in two thousand six. The Wii was released on November nineteenth, two thousand six in North America, and in December for most other regions. Instead of chasing the most powerful graphics, it used motion controls that let anyone swing a remote like a tennis racket. Wii Sports, which came in the box in most regions, sold close to eighty three million copies, according to Wikipedia's list of best selling video games. The console brought grandparents, parents and kids into gaming together. It competed with the Xbox three sixty and the PlayStation Three, and it proved that fun and an easy design could beat raw power. That lesson would come back later.

sections.heading: The Nintendo Switch era
sections.script: The Nintendo Switch launched worldwide on March third, two thousand seventeen. It is a hybrid, so you can play it on a television, as a tablet, or as a handheld. In early twenty twenty six, Nintendo reported that as of December thirty first, twenty twenty five, the Switch had sold one hundred fifty five point three seven million units, passing the Nintendo DS at one hundred fifty four point zero two million, to become the best selling Nintendo console ever, as reported by Game Informer and Nintendo Life. That still left it a few million units behind the PlayStation Two. The hybrid idea clearly struck a chord with players around the world.

sections.heading: PlayStation Five, Xbox Series and Switch Two
sections.script: The current generation arrived in November two thousand twenty. The Xbox Series X and Series S were released on November tenth, and the PlayStation Five launched on November twelfth in several regions, and worldwide a week later. Both belong to the ninth generation of consoles. Then, on June fifth, two thousand twenty five, Nintendo launched the Switch Two, with a larger display, more storage and the new Joy Con Two controllers that can act like a mouse. Nintendo reported that the Switch Two had sold seventeen point three million units as of December thirty first, twenty twenty five, and forecast it would pass nineteen million by the end of its fiscal year. A new age of hybrid play is here.

sections.heading: Which console was yours
sections.script: From a black and white box with plastic overlays to a hybrid with a mouse mode controller, the story of consoles is a story of big ideas. Cartridges, discs, online play, motion controls and hybrids all began as bold experiments. So tell us in the comments. Which was the first console you ever played, and which one do you think was the most important in history? Was it the Atari that brought games home, the PlayStation that changed the sound and look of games, or the Switch that took them everywhere? If you enjoyed this timeline, please subscribe to the channel and turn on notifications, because there is much more gaming history on the way.
